title: Presbyterian Church in America v. Louisiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specification 1 was dismissed. On Louisiana Presbytery’s guilty plea to Specification 2, the SJC imposed a public admonition; no further action was ordered.
first_summary: In a BCO 40-5 prosecution arising from Louisiana Presbytery’s handling of concerns about TE Stephen Wilkins, the SJC dismissed Specification 1, holding that the cited procedures were not required steps in the earlier investigation and guilt was not established. On Specification 2, it accepted Presbytery’s guilty plea for failing to find a strong presumption of doctrinal guilt and proceed to trial, and publicly admonished Presbytery. Wilkins’s and his church’s withdrawal made practical amends unavailable.
summary: In this BCO 40-5 proceeding over Louisiana Presbytery’s investigation of TE Stephen Wilkins, the SJC dismissed Specification 1 because it could not find that the cited procedures were constitutionally required or that guilt was proved. The dismissal did not erase concerns about undocumented doctrinal findings; those failures were covered by Specification 2. On Presbytery’s guilty plea to that specification, the SJC imposed a public admonition for failing to find a strong presumption of doctrinal guilt and pursue trial. Wilkins’s and his church’s withdrawal made practical amends unavailable.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption identifies SJC Case 2007-14 (lines 13–14); the decision was approved seriatim and by roll call (lines 107–117).
evidence_notes.dispute: The BCO 40-5 indictment alleged deficient documentation of Wilkins’s doctrinal differences and failure to find a strong presumption of guilt and institute process (lines 23–25).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Specification 1 was dismissed because the cited procedures were not shown to be required and guilt was not established; Specification 2 resulted in admonition upon Presbytery’s guilty plea (lines 50–88).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The dismissal preserved concerns covered by Specification 2, while the withdrawals made practical amends unavailable (lines 66–82). The concurrence and objection were separate writings (lines 119–174).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The decision recounts Case 2006-2 as procedural history (lines 17–23) but does not incorporate another judgment as the operative disposition.
